text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL EXPANDS PROEX EXPORT FINANCE LIST
The Brazilian government on Wednesday announced it would expand as of today the list of goods eligible for special Proex export financing to help small and medium-sized firms.
-- BANKAMERICA EYES BRAZIL'S RETAIL BANKING
Bank of America Chairman and CEO David Coulter on Wednesday said the U.S. bank was looking for opportunities in retail banking in Brazil and other Latin American countries.
-- HSBC TO PAY PREMIUM ON BAMERINDUS IN INSTALLMENTS
HSBC Holdings Plc will be allowed to pay the 380 million reais premium for the acquisition of Banco Bamerindus in seven years, with a grace period of three years.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CIVIL SERVANTS LOSE STABILITY

The Chamber of Deputies gave a first approval to the government's administrative reform. The bill allows state and city governments to fire workers whose jobs are currently protected by the Constitution.
-- POLICEMEN REFUSE TO SPEAK BEFORE DEPUTIES

The 10 policemen accused of beating, intimidating and shooting residents in a poor Sao Paulo neighborhood refused to testify before a legislative inquiry board, based on the Constitution which allows them to speak only in court.
-- SENATORS EXTEND BOND PROBE FOR 45 MORE DAYS
A congressional probe into a multi-million dollar state and municipal debt scam was extended for 45 more days beyond the April 22 deadline.
O GLOBO
-- MARCELLO ADMITS NOT EXPELLING POLICEMEN
After asserting that policemen accused of beating residents should be summarily expelled from the force, Rio de Janeiro state Gov. Marcello Alencar back-tracked, saying they must first be tried.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
